lines.name: Journey to Baan Malur
lines.about: Separate side quests set in the city of Baan Malur and on the Morrowind mainland around it, at Fort Tulis, Cormaris and the craglands to the south. There are six quests to play, plus a ferry service between Morrowind's ports and Raven Rock on Solstheim and one empty placeholder; the records set no level for any of them.

getIn.where: his drinks stall in the Arena Market in Baan Malur, from 8 am for about 12 hours
getIn.how: Get to Baan Malur and talk to Adimmisaru of the Ahemmusa tribe in the Arena Market; he has lost his family amulet and thinks the jeweller Varanie took it.
needs: Reach Baan Malur; the records show a ferry between Raven Rock on Solstheim and Baan Malur

order.what: A placeholder with no objectives and no people; its only text is 'finished quest' and nothing in the records starts it.
You settle the quarrel between Adimmisaru and the jeweller Varanie over his lost amulet, either with Varanie's fake or with the real one from the goblins of Bulwark Krettin.
order.where: Arena Market, Baan Malur, and Bulwark Krettin
order.needs: Reach Baan Malur.

order.what: A guard at Fort Tulis sends you into the depths of the fort to deal with the Bruska goblins, then after the clan's Shaman in Bruska Cave.
order.where: Fort Tulis and Bruska Cave, Morrowind
order.needs: Reach Fort Tulis on the Morrowind mainland.

order.what: Sadren Solis needs wood to build a temple in Cormaris; you get the lumberjack Feldrin's axe back from Llerush Kwama Mine and then look for the ship captain Helvf Blackthorn.
order.where: Cormaris, Cormar Crossing and Llerush Kwama Mine, Morrowind
order.needs: Reach Cormaris.

order.what: The ferry service between Baan Malur, Raven Rock, Cormaris, Llethrin Fel and Pryai; you take a seat on the ferry bench and pick a port. It is a service you can use at any time, not a step in a story.
order.where: the ferry benches at each port

order.what: You take Hlervan's ashes to an elder at the Temple of Reclamations in Baan Malur.
order.where: Temple of Reclamations, Baan Malur
order.needs: Find Hlervan's ashes.

order.what: After you clear Daedra from her basement, the scholar Llynelis sends you after three Daedric keys, then into the Daedric Ruin under Baan Malur, and you confront her at the end.
order.where: Llynelis Manor, Baan Malur; Ashimmidarum; Dunnashammipuri; near Cormaris
order.needs: Reach Baan Malur.

order.what: Kar-Jei, leader of an Argonian camp, asks you to free his people from Dres slavers and to steal military documents from Fort Blacklight without being seen.
order.where: Saxhleel Camp, in the craglands south of Baan Malur; the Dres Slaver's Camp; Fort Blacklight, Baan Malur
order.needs: Find the Saxhleel Camp south of Baan Malur.

options: Give Adimmisaru Varanie's fake amulet: if he believes you the quest is done and Varanie pays you a bonus; if he doesn't, the quest fails
Bring back the real amulet from Bulwark Krettin: Adimmisaru pays you
Sell the real amulet to Varanie: the quest fails
Kill Adimmisaru or Varanie: the quarrel ends and the quest completes
Kill Llynelis when you confront her
Spare Llynelis
Stay loyal and bring the documents to Kar-Jei: Redoran soldiers raid the camp, and if Kar-Jei lives he gives you his Naming-Knife
Sell the Saxhleel out to the Redoran captain at Fort Blacklight: Redoran soldiers raid the camp
Sell the Saxhleel out to the Dres Captain at the slaver camp: Dres slavers raid the camp

gives: Kar-Jei's Naming Knife (dagger), if you stay loyal in The Struggle for Justice
Ferry travel between Baan Malur, Raven Rock, Cormaris, Llethrin Fel and Pryai
closes: Adimmisaru or Varanie dies if you choose to kill one of them in The Amulet of Old
Llynelis dies if you choose to kill her in Daedra and Deceit
The Bruska Pogrom fails if the guard at Fort Tulis dies
The Struggle for Justice fails if Kar-Jei is killed in the raid on the Saxhleel Camp

unsure.why: No quest in this line carries a level gate, and no dungeon's level range is in the checked reads, so the level it is made for isn't known.

The quests have no shared start; The Amulet of Old is the line's opening in the start records, but any of the others can be found first. Which route a new player should take to Baan Malur (the Raven Rock ferry or the Dwemer ruin Kalbthurz a book names as a way through) isn't set out in the records.
A Grand Venture is a bare placeholder; whether a script ever runs it isn't shown.
The New Temple's journal after you find Helvf Blackthorn is the author's placeholder notes with no objectives, so the later part may be unfinished.
The ferry checks something before offering Llethrin Fel, Pryai and Vivec, so those routes may need unlocking; how you book a crossing isn't in the records.
Bruska Shaman's Staff (a lightning staff) is linked to the Bruska Shaman only by its name; the other rewards are leveled lists or gold whose contents aren't in the records.
The sell-out endings of The Struggle for Justice have no ending marked in the journal; what happens to Kar-Jei and whether you are paid isn't in the records.

lines.name: Siege at Icemoth
lines.about: A short dungeon story on the Hjorkvild Isles, frozen islands north of Jehanna, where a necromancer holds the old Imperial fort Fort Icemoth with an army of undead, and a Nord barrow on the main island lies beyond it. Fort Icemoth is a level 24 to 50 dungeon and Winter Shroud Sanctum level 30 to 55; the line has two dungeon quests and two book quests.

getIn.where: by a beached sailboat on the coast
getIn.how: Read the Waterlogged Journal the dead mercenary carries; it tells of Fort Icemoth, an old Imperial fort on frozen islands north of Jehanna full of undead, and the quest sends you there.

order.quest: Black Book: The Font of Memory
order.what: Reading the Black Book 'The Font of Memory' pulls you into Apocrypha to learn the knowledge hidden in it.
order.where: Apocrypha
order.needs: Find the Black Book 'The Font of Memory'.

order.what: The book 'The Caches of Skorjan Iron-Beard' sends you to the Old Wooden Jetty to find a hidden cache, with a dead mercenary nearby.
order.where: the Old Wooden Jetty
order.needs: Find and read 'The Caches of Skorjan Iron-Beard'.

order.what: You travel to Fort Icemoth and deal with the source of the undead, the Breton necromancer Silas Marceau.
order.where: Fort Icemoth, Hjorkvild Isles
order.needs: Read the Waterlogged Journal.

order.what: Silas Marceau's journal mentions a topaz dragon claw; you find it among his things and use it to open the portcullis in Winter Shroud Sanctum, a Nord barrow on the main island.
order.where: Fort Icemoth and Winter Shroud Sanctum, Hjorkvild Isles
order.needs: Reach Silas Marceau's belongings at Fort Icemoth.

gives: The boss chests of Fort Icemoth and Winter Shroud Sanctum
closes: Silas Marceau is killed at Fort Icemoth
The dragon priest Tovinaan is fought at the end of Winter Shroud Sanctum

unsure.why: The beach with the sailboat is in a coastal cell the records don't name. The dead mercenary near the Old Wooden Jetty in Caches of Skorjan Iron-Beard may be the same body, but no record ties them.
How you cross to the Hjorkvild Isles isn't spelled out; the sailboat is part of the quest but the records don't show it carrying you.

Where the Black Book lies isn't in the records; the mod's Black Book setup quest is tied to Winter Shroud Sanctum, so it is probably there. Whether Apocrypha needs Dragonborn progress first isn't shown.
Where copies of 'The Caches of Skorjan Iron-Beard' are found, the Old Wooden Jetty's hold, and what is in the cache aren't in the records.
The dragon priest mask Tovinaan is in the mod, but the records don't put it on the dragon priest or tie it to The Topaz Claw.

The Omen of Gluttony, Omen of Immobility and Omen of Warding powers carry this mod's Black Book names, but the records don't tie them to the Black Book quest's ending or say whether you get all three or pick one.

lines.name: The Gray Cowl of Nocturnal
lines.about: A vision sends you to the Hall of the Initiation in Skyrim, and the Gray Cowl story then takes you through the Imperial City Prison, Sancre Tor and Coldharbour to the Alik'r Desert in Hammerfell, where you claim the Gray Cowl from a mausoleum. Reaching the desert also opens Betalille's Hammerfell quests in Ben Erai, Salas Kazas and the Wind Scour Temple; there are 40 quests in all, no level gate is set, and the desert's dungeons hold enemies from level 10 to 80.

getIn.where: wherever you are; the vision points you to the Hall of the Initiation in Skyrim
getIn.how: The quest runs from the start of the game: you have a strange vision, and the quest marker shows you the way to the Hall of the Initiation, whose door needs the Key to Hall of the Initiation.

order.needs: Be partway through The Call of Gray Cowl of Nocturnal.

order.where: Shanta Filibb and Ben Erai, Alik'r Desert

unsure.why: No quest in the line carries a level gate; the level range is taken from the desert dungeons in the checked reads (Al Shedim 10 to 80, Khenzedum 15 to 60, Sadraaka level 40).

The quest is set to run from game start with no conditions; what moves it to the vision (a level, a time, a script) isn't in the records. Where the Key to Hall of the Initiation comes from, and which hold the Hall of the Initiation and Seviana's House stand in, aren't shown.
The Betalille quests are all in the Alik'r Desert, which The Call of Gray Cowl of Nocturnal takes you to; whether From Solstheim to Hammerfell is another way in isn't in the records.
The Call of Gray Cowl of Nocturnal probably takes you to Akavir near the end (a portal alias and Seviana's line about Hammerfell and Akavir); those stages have no text.

Time for the Farewells has no giver or start event in the records; it most likely follows the end of The Call of Gray Cowl of Nocturnal, and that Seviana and Luvien leave Skyrim for good is read from its title.
Helping the Enemy most likely comes after The Ash'abah (Honai's later packages assume it is done), but no condition says so.
The Dark Brotherhood in Hammerfell may need you to be in the Dark Brotherhood with the Dawnstar Sanctuary open; the conditions on the Unknown Initiate's line aren't in the records.
The order of Jukka's four museum quests and Tenerio's contracts is read from their journals; the conditions that unlock each one aren't in the records.

The six Dragonguard Archives books have no giver or start event; they probably start from a notice or note and probably come after A Lost Temple in Hammerfell, since the archive chest is in the Wind Scour Temple.
Where the Alik'r Desert Sanctuary, the Ash'abah Hideout, Vulstad, Arenar's Camp and most other desert places lie isn't in the places records.
Whether Ending the Dark Brotherhood in Hammerfell again ends Tenerio's contracts is read from its aliases; it swaps in a separate hostile Tenerio, and the script isn't read.

Many rewards are quest script properties not confirmed by a log line: the Left Eye of Coldharbour, the Unlock Container tome, Irlav's Penitence (what it does isn't in the item records), Respected by the Ash'abah (its effect isn't given), the Crimson Eviscerator from Leollus, and the gold amounts.
What triggers the failure of Memories of the Umbranox isn't in the records; that a missed journal is gone for good is a guess from the failure line.

lines.name: The Forgotten City
lines.about: A mystery in a hidden Dwarven city beneath ruins in the Reach, which you enter to look for Cassia's younger brother Altrius. It has two quests, the second played out inside the first, and the records set no level for it.

getIn.where: inside the Forgotten Ruins, hidden Dwarven ruins in the Reach
getIn.how: A courier hands you a letter, Cassia's Plea; read it and travel to the ruins in the Reach, where Cassia waits near the entrance. If you find the ruins on your own first, the quest starts there.

order.what: Cassia asks you to find her brother Altrius; you take a leap of faith into the Forgotten City, look for a way out, and finish by bringing Altrius back to her.
order.where: Forgotten Ruins and The Forgotten City, the Reach

order.what: Metellus's portal at the Lakehouse throws you 20 years into the past, and Jarl Metellus asks you to find out which resident will destroy the city.
order.where: the Citadel, the residents' homes and the Underground Tunnels, the Forgotten City
order.needs: Go through the Lakehouse during The Forgotten City.

options: Name a suspect to Jarl Metellus (Domitus, Gulvar, Vernon, Ulrin, Marius, Rykas or Deglund), and he asks you to lure them into the Underground Tunnels and kill them
Accuse Metellus himself, or admit that you are the threat
Refuse to kill your suspect and find your own way back to your time
Win the Arbiter over, who returns you to your own time; this is the ending that completes The Forgotten City
Back in the present with Altrius alive, smash the cracked wall in the Citadel bathroom and escort him out of the city
Convince the Arbiter to wind back the Dwarves' Law, bring Altrius to Cassia, and she rewards you and enters the city

gives: The Immaculate Dwarven Armor set (Armor, Helmet, Boots and Gauntlets), heavy armor that makes you immune to radiation when all four are worn
closes: The suspect you name to Metellus can be killed in the Underground Tunnels
Forget-me-not fails if Metellus kills himself to make his portal and you are left with no way back except through it

unsure.why: No level gate is in the records; the line carries an average Speech check, but which conversation uses it isn't shown.
What makes the courier arrive (a level, a place, a time) isn't in the records, and the ruins' entrance stands in an exterior cell the places records don't name; 'the Reach' is the journal's wording.

The escort-Altrius-out ending finishes Cassia's business in the journal but isn't flagged as completing The Forgotten City; only the Arbiter ending is. No stage of Forget-me-not is marked as completing it.
Cassia's reward is probably the Treasure Hunter's Talisman (an amulet, 50% greater chance of finding special treasure), whose record marks it as hers, but nothing hands it over in the records.

The armor is named from Rykas and the helmet from the Underground Tunnels; where the Boots and Gauntlets are found, and how each piece is handed over, isn't decoded. The Arbiter's Helmet is in the records, but where you get it isn't shown.

lines.name: Gravewind
lines.about: A story that starts at an abandoned homestead among graves and strange flowers in the Falkreath woods and leads into Gravewind, another realm reached through the house. It has three quests; the vampire lair that holds the key to the homestead has a boss leveled 55 to 125, and no other level gate is set.

getIn.who: Vighar, the vampire who carries the key
getIn.where: Bloodlet Throne in Falkreath for the key; the homestead is in the woods of Falkreath
getIn.how: Kill the vampire Vighar in Bloodlet Throne for the Cemetery Homestead Key, then unlock the abandoned homestead in the Falkreath woods and explore it.
needs: Cemetery Homestead Key, carried by Vighar in Bloodlet Throne (LoreRim puts this lock on the homestead's door)

order.what: Touching the light Richter left in Gravewind brings the realm down, and you have to escape before it falls.
order.where: Gravewind
order.needs: Reach Richter's light in Gravewind, through In the Pines and Lost in the Woods.

order.what: You unlock the abandoned homestead in the Falkreath woods and explore it; the door locks behind you and you have to find a way out.
order.where: Bloodlet Throne for the key; Cemetery Homestead, Falkreath
order.needs: The Cemetery Homestead Key from Vighar.

order.what: You step out of the homestead into a land that isn't Falkreath, follow the notes of a man named Richter through Gravewind's underground city, and find your way home.
order.where: Gravewind and Gravewind Depths
order.needs: Finish In the Pines.

options: Touch Richter's light: Gravewind falls, the souls enthralled there are freed, and the house in the Falkreath woods is gone for good
Leave the light alone: Lost to Oblivion doesn't start and Gravewind stays as Lost in the Woods leaves it

gives: Lifesurge, a power: once a day, scarlet lightning completely restores your health
Herrah's Axe and her life-stealing Scarlet Cloak, named in the journal at the end of Lost in the Woods
Gravewind itself, left to you at the end of Lost in the Woods
Death Strider, at the end of Lost to Oblivion
closes: Herrah, the Wraithmother of Gravewind, is consumed by the void at the end of Lost in the Woods
Lost to Oblivion destroys Gravewind and the house in the Falkreath woods for good

unsure.why: The homestead's door stays hidden until another object is enabled, and what enables it isn't in the records. LoreRim's lock also edits Dark Ancestor, the quest whose alias holds Vighar; whether Vighar is in Bloodlet Throne without Dark Ancestor running isn't shown. Dengeir of Stuhn in Falkreath gives Dark Ancestor.
Richter's light is probably Richter's Flame in The Way Home, the last stretch of Lost in the Woods; whether Lost in the Woods must be finished before Lost to Oblivion isn't shown.

Herrah's Axe and the Scarlet Cloak are named only in the journal's last entry and nothing hands them over; the Infused Battleaxe is the mod's only battleaxe and may be her Axe, and no cloak from the mod is in the item records.
Death Strider is given through a script property named for a perk; its effect isn't in the spell or power records.
The power Expel Greater Spirit lets you expel the soul once trapped in the Gravewind Sentinel, but nothing ties it to Lost in the Woods.
